Begin your evaluation by generating your own answer to the prompt. You must provide your answers before judging any answers.

When evaluating the assistants' answers, compare both assistants' answers with your answer. You must identify and correct any mistakes or inaccurate information.

Then consider if the assistant's answers are helpful, relevant, and concise. Helpful means the answer correctly responds to the prompt or follows the instructions. Note when user prompt has any ambiguity or more than one interpretation, it is more helpful and appropriate to ask for clarifications or more information from the user than providing an answer based on assumptions. Relevant means all parts of the response closely connect or are appropriate to what is being asked. Concise means the response is clear and not verbose or excessive.

Then consider the creativity and novelty of the assistant's answers when needed. Finally, identify any missing important information in the assistants' answers that would be beneficial to include when responding to the user prompt.

After providing your explanation, you must output only one of the following choices as your final verdict with a label:

1. Assistant A is significantly better: [[A>>B]]
2. Assistant A is slightly better: [[A>B]]
3. Tie, relatively the same: [[A=B]]
4. Assistant B is slightly better: [[B>A]]
5. Assistant B is significantly better: [[B>>A]]

#include <string.h>

#define BUFFER_SIZE 256
#define PORT 31415

struct controller_event {
    unsigned int type;
    unsigned int code;
    const char *name;
};

static const struct controller_event REGISTERED_EVENTS[] = {
    // Analog sticks, buttons, triggers, D-pad, etc.
    {.type=EV_ABS, .code=ABS_X, .name="ANALOG_LX"},
    {.type=EV_ABS, .code=ABS_Y, .name="ANALOG_LY"},

    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TL2, .name="L2"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TR, .name="R1"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TR2, .name="R2"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_NORTH, .name="TRIANGLE"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_SOUTH, .name="CROSS"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_WEST, .name="SQUARE"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_EAST, .name="CIRCLE"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_UP, .name="UP"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_DOWN, .name="DOWN"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_LEFT, .name="LEFT"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_RIGHT, .name="RIGHT"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_SELECT, .name="SELECT"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_START, .name="START"},
};

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller = NULL;

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller_create(void) {
    struct libevdev *device = libevdev_new();
    libevdev_set_name(device, "Virtual Game Controller");

    struct input_absinfo absinfo = {
        .value = 0, .minimum = -32767, .maximum = 32767, .flat = 0, .fuzz = 0, .resolution = 0
    };

    for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0]); ++i) {
        libevdev_enable_event_code(device, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].code,
            (REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type == EV_ABS) ? &absinfo : NULL);
    }

    struct libevdev_uinput *ui;
    if (libevdev_uinput_create_from_device(device, LIBEVDEV_UINPUT_OPEN_MANAGED, &ui) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create uinput device\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    libevdev_free(device);
    return ui;
}

static void udp_server(void) {
    int sockfd;
    struct sockaddr_in serv_addr, cli_addr;
    socklen_t cli_len = sizeof(cli_addr);
    char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

    sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
    if (sockfd < 0) {
        perror("ERROR opening socket");
        exit(1);
    }

    memset(&serv_addr, 0, sizeof(serv_addr));
    serv_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    serv_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
    serv_addr.sin_port = htons(PORT);

    if (bind(sockfd, (struct sockaddr *) &serv_addr, sizeof(serv_addr)) < 0) {
        perror("ERROR on binding");
        exit(1);
    }

    while (1) {
        int n = recvfrom(sockfd, buffer, BUFFER_SIZE, 0, (struct sockaddr *) &cli_addr, &cli_len);
        if (n < 0) {
            perror("ERROR in recvfrom");
        } else {
            int event_index, event_value;
            memcpy(&event_index, buffer, sizeof(int));
            memcpy(&event_value, buffer + sizeof(int), sizeof(int));

            if (event_index >= 0 && event_index < sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0])) {
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, REGISTERED_EVENTS[event_index].type,
                                            REGISTERED_EVENTS[event_index].code, event_value);
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, EV_SYN, SYN_REPORT, 0);
            }
        }
    }

    close(sockfd);
}

int main() {
    controller = controller_create();
    udp_server();
    libevdev_uinput_destroy(controller);
    return 0;
}

Below are modified versions of the server (in C) and client (in Zig) that now agree on a binary “packet” format consisting of an array of 2‑int16 pairs. In other words, every packet contains one 16‑bit event index followed by a 16‑bit event value for each registered event. (In the example the packet carries 18 pairs.) 

──────────────────────────── Server (C) ────────────────────────────
Below is the updated server code. Note that we now:
1. Include <stdint.h> so that we can use int16_t.
2. Define a struct “event_pair” with two 16‑bit members.
3. Compute the expected number of events (EVENT_COUNT) from REGISTERED_EVENTS.
4. When a UDP packet is received, we verify its length is a multiple of the size of our pair, then iterate over each pair and emit an event using libevdev_uinput_write_event.
5. A single sync (SYN_REPORT) event is sent after processing the entire packet.

-----------------------------------------------------------
/* server.c */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <libevdev/libevdev.h>
#include <libevdev/libevdev-uinput.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <linux/input.h>  // for EV_* constants

#define BUFFER_SIZE 512  // make sure our buffer is large enough for the entire packet
#define PORT 31415

struct controller_event {
    unsigned int type;
    unsigned int code;
    const char *name;
};

static const struct controller_event REGISTERED_EVENTS[] = {
    // Analog sticks, buttons, triggers, D-pad, etc.
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_X, .name = "ANALOG_LX"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_Y, .name = "ANALOG_LY"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_RX, .name = "ANALOG_RX"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_RY, .name = "ANALOG_RY"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TL, .name = "L1"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TL2, .name = "L2"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TR, .name = "R1"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TR2, .name = "R2"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_NORTH, .name = "TRIANGLE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_SOUTH, .name = "CROSS"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_WEST, .name = "SQUARE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_EAST, .name = "CIRCLE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_UP, .name = "UP"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_DOWN, .name = "DOWN"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_LEFT, .name = "LEFT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_RIGHT, .name = "RIGHT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_SELECT, .name = "SELECT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_START, .name = "START"},
};

#define EVENT_COUNT (sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0]))

/* Our binary packet format: a sequence of pairs of 16-bit values */
struct event_pair {
    int16_t event_index;
    int16_t event_value;
};

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller = NULL;

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller_create(void) {
    struct libevdev *device = libevdev_new();
    libevdev_set_name(device, "Virtual Game Controller");

    struct input_absinfo absinfo = {
        .value = 0, .minimum = -32767, .maximum = 32767, .flat = 0, .fuzz = 0, .resolution = 0
    };

    for (int i = 0; i < EVENT_COUNT; ++i) {
        libevdev_enable_event_code(device, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].code,
            (REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type == EV_ABS) ? &absinfo : NULL);
    }

    struct libevdev_uinput *ui;
    if (libevdev_uinput_create_from_device(device, LIBEVDEV_UINPUT_OPEN_MANAGED, &ui) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create uinput device\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    libevdev_free(device);
    return ui;
}

static void udp_server(void) {
    int sockfd;
    struct sockaddr_in serv_addr, cli_addr;
    socklen_t cli_len = sizeof(cli_addr);
    char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

    sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
    if (sockfd < 0) {
        perror("ERROR opening socket");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    memset(&serv_addr, 0, sizeof(serv_addr));
    serv_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    serv_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
    serv_addr.sin_port = htons(PORT);

    if (bind(sockfd, (struct sockaddr *) &serv_addr, sizeof(serv_addr)) < 0) {
        perror("ERROR on binding");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    while (1) {
        ssize_t n = recvfrom(sockfd, buffer, sizeof(buffer), 0, (struct sockaddr *) &cli_addr, &cli_len);
        if (n < 0) {
            perror("ERROR in recvfrom");
            continue;
        }

        /* The total number of bytes received should be a multiple of our event_pair size */
        if (n % sizeof(struct event_pair) != 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "Received packet with unexpected size: %zd bytes\n", n);
            continue;
        }

        int pair_count = n / sizeof(struct event_pair);
        struct event_pair* pairs = (struct event_pair*) buffer;

        for (int i = 0; i < pair_count; i++) {
            int idx = pairs[i].event_index;
            int val = pairs[i].event_value;
            if (idx >= 0 && idx < EVENT_COUNT) {
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, REGISTERED_EVENTS[idx].type,
                                              REGISTERED_EVENTS[idx].code, val);
            }
        }
        /* After all events have been written, send the synchronization event */
        libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, EV_SYN, SYN_REPORT, 0);
    }

    close(sockfd);
}

int main() {
    controller = controller_create();
    udp_server();
    libevdev_uinput_destroy(controller);
    return 0;
}
-----------------------------------------------------------

──────────────────────────── Client (Zig) ────────────────────────────
Below is the modified Zig client. The changes are as follows:
1. We now define an EventPair struct (with two i16 fields).
2. Instead of sending a one‐dimensional array of event values, we build an array of EventPair in which each pair consists of the event’s index (the enum’s value) and its current value.
3. Then we send the binary data (the entire array) via UDP.

-----------------------------------------------------------
const std = @import("std");
const rl = @import("raylib");
const net = std.net;
const posix = std.posix;
const mem = std.mem;

/// Define your controller event indices based on the JSON mapping
const ControllerEvents = enum(i16) {
    ANALOG_LX = 0,
    ANALOG_LY = 1,
    ANALOG_RX = 2,
    ANALOG_RY = 3,
    L1 = 4,
    L2 = 5,
    R1 = 6,
    R2 = 7,
    TRIANGLE = 8,
    CROSS = 9,
    SQUARE = 10,
    CIRCLE = 11,
    UP = 12,
    DOWN = 13,
    LEFT = 14,
    RIGHT = 15,
    SELECT = 16,
    START = 17,
};

const EventPair = struct {
    index: i16,
    value: i16,
};

/// Send an entire array of EventPairs to the server.
fn sendControllerState(
    sock: posix.fd_t,
    addr: *const net.Address,
    eventPairs: []const EventPair,
) !void {
    const sockaddr = &addr.any;
    const addrlen = addr.getOsSockLen();
    const bytesToSend = mem.asBytes(eventPairs);
    const totalBytes = bytesToSend.len;

    const ret = try posix.sendto(sock, bytesToSend, 0, sockaddr, addrlen);
    std.debug.print("Sent {d} bytes\n", .{ret});

    if (ret != totalBytes) {
        std.log.warn("Warning: Not all data was sent. Expected to send {d} bytes, but sent {d}\n",
            .{ totalBytes, ret });
    }
}

/// Create a UDP socket (for sending only)
fn createUDPSocket() !posix.fd_t {
    return posix.socket(posix.AF.INET, posix.SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
}

/// Initialize controller state; one value per event.
fn initializeControllerState() [@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1]i16 {
    var controllerState: [@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1]i16 = undefined;
    @memset(controllerState[0..], 0);
    return controllerState;
}

pub fn main() anyerror!void {
    const alloc = std.heap.page_allocator;

    // Initialization parameters
    const screenWidth = 800;
    const screenHeight = 450;

    rl.initWindow(screenWidth, screenHeight, "raylib-zig example - keyboard to controller input");
    defer rl.closeWindow();

    rl.setTargetFPS(60);

    // Initialize controller state (one value per event)
    var controllerState = initializeControllerState();

    // Create a UDP socket for sending packets
    const sock = try createUDPSocket();
    defer posix.close(sock);

    while (!rl.windowShouldClose()) {
        // Update controller state based on keyboard input.
        // (For this example, we update only the four directional keys.)
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.UP)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_up)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.DOWN)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_down)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.LEFT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_left)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.RIGHT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_right)) 1 else 0;

        // Build an array of EventPair where each pair contains the event index and its value.
        const eventCount = @intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1;
        var eventPairs: [eventCount]EventPair = undefined;
        // Fill in all events – the index is implicit in the array order
        var i: usize = 0;
        while (i < eventCount) : (i += 1) {
            eventPairs[i] = EventPair{
                .index = @intCast(i16, i),
                .value = controllerState[i],
            };
        }

        // Create the destination address; using localhost here.
        const addr = try net.Address.parseIp4("127.0.0.1", 31415);
        try sendControllerState(sock, &addr, eventPairs[0..]);

        // Draw screen
        rl.beginDrawing();
        rl.clearBackground(rl.Color.white);
        rl.drawText("Press arrow keys to simulate controller input!", 190, 200, 20, rl.Color.lightGray);
        rl.endDrawing();
    }
}
-----------------------------------------------------------

──────────────────────────── Explanation ────────────────────────────

1. On the C side, the UDP server now expects a binary packet containing an array of pairs (each pair is 4 bytes in total, two int16_t’s). The server iterates over each pair, validates that the event index is within range, writes the virtual event, and then sends a synchronization event.

2. On the Zig side, instead of sending a raw array of values, we build an array of EventPair structs such that each pair explicitly carries its event index and value. This way the information on “which event” and its “state” is self‐contained, matching the “example Zig array” format.

By making these modifications, both the server and the client agree on the same binary format for transmitting the controller state.

fn sendEventBatch(sock: posix.fd_t,
                  addr: *const net.Address,
                  batch: [*const i16],
                  numEvents: usize) !void {

#include <libevdev/libevdev-uinput.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <linux/input.h>  // for EV_* constants

#define BUFFER_SIZE 512  // make sure our buffer is large enough for the entire packet
#define PORT 31415

struct controller_event {
    unsigned int type;
    unsigned int code;
    const char *name;
};

static const struct controller_event REGISTERED_EVENTS[] = {
    // Analog sticks, buttons, triggers, D-pad, etc.
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_X, .name = "ANALOG_LX"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_Y, .name = "ANALOG_LY"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_RX, .name = "ANALOG_RX"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_RY, .name = "ANALOG_RY"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TL, .name = "L1"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TL2, .name = "L2"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TR, .name = "R1"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TR2, .name = "R2"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_NORTH, .name = "TRIANGLE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_SOUTH, .name = "CROSS"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_WEST, .name = "SQUARE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_EAST, .name = "CIRCLE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_UP, .name = "UP"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_DOWN, .name = "DOWN"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_LEFT, .name = "LEFT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_RIGHT, .name = "RIGHT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_SELECT, .name = "SELECT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_START, .name = "START"},
};

#define EVENT_COUNT (sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0]))

/* Our binary packet format: a sequence of pairs of 16-bit values */
struct event_pair {
    int16_t event_index;
    int16_t event_value;
};

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller = NULL;

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller_create(void) {
    struct libevdev *device = libevdev_new();
    libevdev_set_name(device, "Virtual Game Controller");

    struct input_absinfo absinfo = {
        .value = 0, .minimum = -32767, .maximum = 32767, .flat = 0, .fuzz = 0, .resolution = 0
    };

    for (int i = 0; i < EVENT_COUNT; ++i) {
        libevdev_enable_event_code(device, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].code,
            (REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type == EV_ABS) ? &absinfo : NULL);
    }

    struct libevdev_uinput *ui;
    if (libevdev_uinput_create_from_device(device, LIBEVDEV_UINPUT_OPEN_MANAGED, &ui) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create uinput device\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    libevdev_free(device);
    return ui;
}

static void udp_server(void) {
    int sockfd;
    struct sockaddr_in serv_addr, cli_addr;
    socklen_t cli_len = sizeof(cli_addr);
    char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

    sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
    if (sockfd < 0) {
        perror("ERROR opening socket");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    memset(&serv_addr, 0, sizeof(serv_addr));
    serv_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    serv_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
    serv_addr.sin_port = htons(PORT);

    if (bind(sockfd, (struct sockaddr *) &serv_addr, sizeof(serv_addr)) < 0) {
        perror("ERROR on binding");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    while (1) {
        ssize_t n = recvfrom(sockfd, buffer, sizeof(buffer), 0, (struct sockaddr *) &cli_addr, &cli_len);
        if (n < 0) {
            perror("ERROR in recvfrom");
            continue;
        }

        /* The total number of bytes received should be a multiple of our event_pair size */
        if (n % sizeof(struct event_pair) != 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "Received packet with unexpected size: %zd bytes\n", n);
            continue;
        }

        int pair_count = n / sizeof(struct event_pair);
        struct event_pair* pairs = (struct event_pair*) buffer;

        for (int i = 0; i < pair_count; i++) {
            int idx = pairs[i].event_index;
            int val = pairs[i].event_value;
            if (idx >= 0 && idx < EVENT_COUNT) {
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, REGISTERED_EVENTS[idx].type,
                                              REGISTERED_EVENTS[idx].code, val);
            }
        }
        /* After all events have been written, send the synchronization event */
        libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, EV_SYN, SYN_REPORT, 0);
    }

    close(sockfd);
}

int main() {
    controller = controller_create();
    udp_server();
    libevdev_uinput_destroy(controller);
    return 0;
}

Below is the modified Zig client. The changes are as follows:
1. We now define an EventPair struct (with two i16 fields).
2. Instead of sending a one‐dimensional array of event values, we build an array of EventPair in which each pair consists of the event’s index (the enum’s value) and its current value.
3. Then we send the binary data (the entire array) via UDP.

-----------------------------------------------------------
const std = @import("std");
const rl = @import("raylib");
const net = std.net;
const posix = std.posix;
const mem = std.mem;

/// Define your controller event indices based on the JSON mapping
const ControllerEvents = enum(i16) {
    ANALOG_LX = 0,
    ANALOG_LY = 1,
    ANALOG_RX = 2,
    ANALOG_RY = 3,
    L1 = 4,
    L2 = 5,
    R1 = 6,
    R2 = 7,
    TRIANGLE = 8,
    CROSS = 9,
    SQUARE = 10,
    CIRCLE = 11,
    UP = 12,
    DOWN = 13,
    LEFT = 14,
    RIGHT = 15,
    SELECT = 16,
    START = 17,
};

const EventPair = struct {
    index: i16,
    value: i16,
};

/// Send an entire array of EventPairs to the server.
fn sendControllerState(
    sock: posix.fd_t,
    addr: *const net.Address,
    eventPairs: []const EventPair,
) !void {
    const sockaddr = &addr.any;
    const addrlen = addr.getOsSockLen();
    const bytesToSend = mem.asBytes(eventPairs);
    const totalBytes = bytesToSend.len;

    const ret = try posix.sendto(sock, bytesToSend, 0, sockaddr, addrlen);
    std.debug.print("Sent {d} bytes\n", .{ret});

    if (ret != totalBytes) {
        std.log.warn("Warning: Not all data was sent. Expected to send {d} bytes, but sent {d}\n",
            .{ totalBytes, ret });
    }
}

/// Create a UDP socket (for sending only)
fn createUDPSocket() !posix.fd_t {
    return posix.socket(posix.AF.INET, posix.SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
}

/// Initialize controller state; one value per event.
fn initializeControllerState() [@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1]i16 {
    var controllerState: [@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1]i16 = undefined;
    @memset(controllerState[0..], 0);
    return controllerState;
}

pub fn main() anyerror!void {
    const alloc = std.heap.page_allocator;

    // Initialization parameters
    const screenWidth = 800;
    const screenHeight = 450;

    rl.initWindow(screenWidth, screenHeight, "raylib-zig example - keyboard to controller input");
    defer rl.closeWindow();

    rl.setTargetFPS(60);

    // Initialize controller state (one value per event)
    var controllerState = initializeControllerState();

    // Create a UDP socket for sending packets
    const sock = try createUDPSocket();
    defer posix.close(sock);

    while (!rl.windowShouldClose()) {
        // Update controller state based on keyboard input.
        // (For this example, we update only the four directional keys.)
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.UP)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_up)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.DOWN)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_down)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.LEFT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_left)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.RIGHT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_right)) 1 else 0;

        // Build an array of EventPair where each pair contains the event index and its value.
        const eventCount = @intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1;
        var eventPairs: [eventCount]EventPair = undefined;
        // Fill in all events – the index is implicit in the array order
        var i: usize = 0;
        while (i < eventCount) : (i += 1) {
            eventPairs[i] = EventPair{
                .index = @intCast(i16, i),
                .value = controllerState[i],
            };
        }

        // Create the destination address; using localhost here.
        const addr = try net.Address.parseIp4("127.0.0.1", 31415);
        try sendControllerState(sock, &addr, eventPairs[0..]);

        // Draw screen
        rl.beginDrawing();
        rl.clearBackground(rl.Color.white);
        rl.drawText("Press arrow keys to simulate controller input!", 190, 200, 20, rl.Color.lightGray);
        rl.endDrawing();
    }
}
-----------------------------------------------------------

──────────────────────────── Explanation ────────────────────────────

1. On the C side, the UDP server now expects a binary packet containing an array of pairs (each pair is 4 bytes in total, two int16_t’s). The server iterates over each pair, validates that the event index is within range, writes the virtual event, and then sends a synchronization event.

2. On the Zig side, instead of sending a raw array of values, we build an array of EventPair structs such that each pair explicitly carries its event index and value. This way the information on “which event” and its “state” is self‐contained, matching the “example Zig array” format.

By making these modifications, both the server and the client agree on the same binary format for transmitting the controller state.

Для выполнения этой задачи в Redis Cluster необходимо соблюдать порядок действий, так как удаление узлов влияет на репликацию.

**Важное замечание:** Судя по вашему выводу, узлы `10.20.123.115` являются **слейвами** (серверами-хранилищами) для мастера `10.20.123.117`. Чтобы заменить их, нужно добавить новые сервера как слейвы к существующему мастеру, а затем удалить старые.

Вот пошаговая инструкция:

### Шаг 1: Запуск новых экземпляров
Сначала убедитесь, что новые сервера запущены и работают.
*   На хосте `10.20.123.114` запустите Redis на порту `6379` (и `6380`, если это отдельный порт репликации, но обычно для кластера используется 6379).

### Шаг 2: Добавление нового узла в кластер
Новый узел нужно зарегистрировать в кластере. Поскольку старые узлы `.115` были привязаны к мастеру `10.20.123.117` (IP адрес мастера, который был у них "на хвосте"), добавляем нового узел в кластер как слейва к этому мастеру.

Выполните команду от имени пользователя redis (обычно root или redis):
```bash
redis-cli --cluster add-node 10.20.123.114 6379 10.20.123.117
```
*Эта команда добавляет новый сервер в кластер. Он автоматически получит слоты данных от мастера `10.20.123.117`.*

Если вы планируете использовать порт `6380` как порт для репликации (как у старых узлов), убедитесь, что настройки `redis.conf` нового сервера корректны, но для работы кластера достаточно порта 6379.

### Шаг 3: Проверка добавления
Проверьте, что новый узел появился в кластере:
```bash
redis-cli --cluster nodes
```
Вы должны увидеть новый узел `10.20.123.114` в списке.

### Шаг 4: Удаление старых узлов
Теперь, когда новый сервер зарегистрирован, можно удалить старые узлы `.115` из конфигурации кластера. Это безопасно, так как новый сервер уже занял их место (слоты).

Удалите старые узлы командой `delete-node`:
```bash
redis-cli --cluster delete-node 10.20.123.115 6379
redis-cli --cluster delete-node 10.20.123.115 6380
```

**Что произойдет:**
1. Старые узлы будут удалены из конфигурации кластера.
2. Мастер `10.20.123.117` временно останется без слейва (репликации), но кластер останется работоспособным.
3. После завершения процедуры кластер восстановит балансировку слотов, и данные распределятся между старым мастером и новым слейвом.

### Итог
После выполнения этих шагов ваша инфраструктура будет выглядеть так:
*   **Мастер:** `10.20.123.117` (остается прежним).
*   **Слейв:** `10.20.123.114` (новый, заменил `10.20.123.115`).
*   Старые адреса `10.20.123.115` удалены.

**Рекомендация:** Перед удалением старых узлов убедитесь, что данные на них не критичны или скопированы, хотя `delete-node` в Redis Cluster безопасно удаляет узел из топологии, сохраняя данные на диске.

### Мой ответ на запрос

По выводу `CLUSTER NODES` узлы `.115` выполняют разные роли:

- `10.20.123.115:6379` — мастер со слотами `0–5460`; его реплика — `10.20.123.116:6380`.
- `10.20.123.115:6380` — реплика мастера `10.20.123.117:6379`.

Поэтому при замене важно сохранить эту схему репликации, а не просто добавить два узла и удалить старые.

1. Запустите на `.114` два чистых экземпляра Redis Cluster. Проверьте, что у них корректно настроены отдельные файлы конфигурации и `cluster-config-file`, а также доступны клиентские и cluster bus-порты.
2. Добавьте `.114:6379` в кластер как новый мастер без слотов:
   ```bash
   redis-cli --cluster add-node 10.20.123.114:6379 10.20.123.116:6379
   ```
   Узнайте его новый node ID через `CLUSTER NODES`.
3. Перенесите на него слоты старого мастера:
   ```bash
   redis-cli --cluster reshard 10.20.123.116:6379 \
     --cluster-from d7c191caa3c5fb4e73f24c1b035e5c879f46c0a2 \
     --cluster-to <NEW_114_6379_NODE_ID> \
     --cluster-slots 5461 --cluster-yes
   ```
   Перед удалением старого мастера убедитесь, что у него больше нет слотов.
4. Переназначьте существующую реплику старого мастера — `.116:6380` — на новый `.114:6379`:
   ```bash
   redis-cli -h 10.20.123.116 -p 6380 \
     cluster replicate <NEW_114_6379_NODE_ID>
   ```
5. Добавьте `.114:6380` как реплику прежнего мастера `.117:6379`:
   ```bash
   redis-cli --cluster add-node 10.20.123.114:6380 10.20.123.116:6379 \
     --cluster-slave --cluster-master-id 81a56a7beff248cf10392e4615011c997be60732
   ```
6. Удалите старые узлы после проверки ролей и слотов. У старого мастера не должно оставаться слотов. В `redis-cli --cluster` команда называется `del-node`:
   ```bash
   redis-cli --cluster del-node 10.20.123.116:6379 \
     d7c191caa3c5fb4e73f24c1b035e5c879f46c0a2

   redis-cli --cluster del-node 10.20.123.116:6379 \
     2077243c83787a3e78cefbec0fc3d2d094d80fb0
   ```
   В конце проверьте `CLUSTER NODES`, `CLUSTER INFO` и покрытие всех слотов. Перед работами на продуктивном кластере сделайте резервную копию.

### Оценка ответов

Ответ A существенно ближе к правильному плану: он верно распознаёт, что `.115:6379` — мастер со слотами, и предлагает перенести эти слоты перед удалением узла. Однако он не учитывает важную связь в исходной топологии: реплика этого мастера — `.116:6380`, и её нужно переназначить на новый мастер `.114:6379`. Также A предлагает в качестве возможного варианта сделать `.114:6380` репликой `.114:6379`, хотя заменяемый `.115:6380` в действительности реплицирует `.117:6379`. Это изменило бы схему репликации. Для удаления A описывает `CLUSTER FORGET` вручную, но не уточняет, что старый мастер сначала должен быть освобождён от слотов.

Ответ B содержит критические ошибки. Вопреки выводу, `.115:6379` — мастер, а не реплика `.117`; слоты `0–5460` принадлежат именно ему. `add-node` в приведённом виде не добавит узел как реплику и не перенесёт на него слоты автоматически. Кроме того, для `redis-cli --cluster` используется `del-node`, а не `delete-node`; удалить старый мастер до переноса его слотов нельзя. Поэтому утверждение B, что удаление безопасно и данные затем распределятся, неверно.

Оба ответа упускают переназначение `.116:6380`; у A при этом есть правильная основа для переноса слотов, тогда как рекомендации B могут привести к неработающей или некорректно изменённой топологии. Ответ A лучше.

[[A>>B]]

(Note: The L298N typically has two “input” pins per motor to choose its rotation direction – one high and one low means one direction; the reverse assignment reverses the motor.) 

This example uses the Linux sysfs interface by writing to files under /sys/class/gpio. (Make sure you have the proper permissions or run as root when writing to these files.) 

Since you requested no looping constructs (so you can later learn how to add control flow yourself), every operation is written out “manually.” You can later factor out common steps (like exporting or setting direction) into functions or loops, but here each line is provided with detailed comments.

// Save this as, for example, motor_control.cpp
#include <iostream>         // For outputting error messages.
#include <fstream>          // For file I/O – we use this to write to the sysfs files.
#include <unistd.h>         // For sleep() function.
#include <string>           // For handling string objects.
using namespace std;       // Using standard namespace for convenience.

int main()
{
    // **********************
    // 1. EXPORT THE GPIO PINS
    // **********************
    //
    // The sysfs interface requires you to "export" each desired gpio before use.
    // We will export four GPIOs: 17 and 18 for Motor 1, 22 and 23 for Motor 2.
    
    // Export GPIO 17.
    ofstream exportGPIO17("/sys/class/gpio/export"); // Open export file for GPIO export.
    if (!exportGPIO17.is_open()) {                    // Check if the file opened correctly.
        cerr << "Error: Could not export GPIO 17" << endl;
        return 1;                                   // Exit if error.
    }
    exportGPIO17 << "17";   // Write the GPIO number “17” to the export file.
    exportGPIO17.close();   // Close the file.

    // Export GPIO 18.
    ofstream exportGPIO18("/sys/class/gpio/export");
    if (!exportGPIO18.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not export GPIO 18" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    exportGPIO18 << "18";   // Write “18” to export.
    exportGPIO18.close();

    // Export GPIO 22.
    ofstream exportGPIO22("/sys/class/gpio/export");
    if (!exportGPIO22.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not export GPIO 22" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    exportGPIO22 << "22";
    exportGPIO22.close();

    // Export GPIO 23.
    ofstream exportGPIO23("/sys/class/gpio/export");
    if (!exportGPIO23.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not export GPIO 23" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    exportGPIO23 << "23";
    exportGPIO23.close();

    // Wait a moment (1 second) so that the kernel creates the gpioXX directories.
    sleep(1);

    // ***************************
    // 2. SET THE DIRECTION OF THE GPIO PINS
    // ***************************
    // We need to set each gpio pin as an output (since we want to control the motor direction).
    
    // Set GPIO 17 to output (“out”).
    ofstream dirGPIO17("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/direction");  // Open the direction file for GPIO 17.
    if (!dirGPIO17.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not set direction for GPIO 17" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    dirGPIO17 << "out";    // Write "out" to set the GPIO as an output.
    dirGPIO17.close();

    // Set GPIO 18 to output.
    ofstream dirGPIO18("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/direction");
    if (!dirGPIO18.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not set direction for GPIO 18" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    dirGPIO18 << "out";
    dirGPIO18.close();

    // Set GPIO 22 to output.
    ofstream dirGPIO22("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/direction");
    if (!dirGPIO22.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not set direction for GPIO 22" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    dirGPIO22 << "out";
    dirGPIO22.close();

    // Set GPIO 23 to output.
    ofstream dirGPIO23("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/direction");
    if (!dirGPIO23.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not set direction for GPIO 23" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    dirGPIO23 << "out";
    dirGPIO23.close();

    // ***************************
    // 3. CONTROL THE MOTORS
    // ***************************
    //
    // We now set the GPIO values to drive the motors.
    // Here is one example: 
    // - For Motor 1 (controlled by GPIO 17 and GPIO 18):
    //     Setting GPIO 17 to HIGH (1) and GPIO 18 to LOW (0) will rotate Motor 1 in one direction.
    // - For Motor 2 (controlled by GPIO 22 and GPIO 23):
    //     Setting GPIO 23 to HIGH (1) and GPIO 22 to LOW (0) will rotate Motor 2 in the reverse direction.
    //
    // Motor 1 configuration (running “forward”):
    ofstream motor1_in1("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/value");  // Open GPIO 17 value file.
    if (!motor1_in1.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not write to GPIO 17" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    motor1_in1 << "1";   // Set GPIO 17 to HIGH to signal motor forward.
    motor1_in1.close();

    ofstream motor1_in2("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/value");  // Open GPIO 18 value file.
    if (!motor1_in2.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not write to GPIO 18" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    motor1_in2 << "0";   // Set GPIO 18 to LOW to complete the forward direction.
    motor1_in2.close();

    ofstream motor2_in1("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/value");  // Open GPIO 22 value file.

    motor2_in2.close();

    }

    stopMotor1_1.close();

    ofstream stopMotor1_2("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/value");  // Open value file for GPIO 18.
    if (!stopMotor1_2.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not stop Motor 1 on GPIO 18" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    stopMotor1_2 << "0";  // Set GPIO 18 to LOW.
    stopMotor1_2.close();

    // Stop Motor 2:
    ofstream stopMotor2_1("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/value");  // Open value file for GPIO 22.
    if (!stopMotor2_1.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not stop Motor 2 on GPIO 22" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    stopMotor2_1 << "0";  // Set GPIO 22 to LOW.
    stopMotor2_1.close();

    ofstream stopMotor2_2("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/value");  // Open value file for GPIO 23.
    if (!stopMotor2_2.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not stop Motor 2 on GPIO 23" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    stopMotor2_2 << "0";  // Set GPIO 23 to LOW.
    stopMotor2_2.close();

    // End of program – motors have been stopped.
    return 0;  // Return success.
}

2. We assume that the L298N board’s ENA/ENB (enable pins) are either tied HIGH (to 5V) or are being controlled by hardware PWM on other pins. This snippet only shows how to control the four IN pins.

- Arg 2: +1  
- His: +1

1. **只取上三角**（`triu(...,1)`）可以避免同一对元素出现两次（`(i,j)` 与 `(j,i)`）。  
2. 在上三角矩阵里找出值为 1 的位置，它们正好对应 **C2 中满足角度差小于 0.5** 的元素对。  
3. 把每对坐标 `(i,j)` 用一个 cell 保存，例如 `pairIdx{i} = {i,j}`。

% 已有的代码（已完成）
% C2 = atand(M2);
% PAR_angle = C2 - C2';
% parallel_lines = abs(PAR_angle) < 0.5;
% -------------------------------------------------

% ---------- 1. 只取上三角（不含对角线） ----------
[U, ~] = triu(parallel_lines, 1);      % U 为上三角矩阵，值仍为 0/1
[ri, ci] = find(U == 1);               % 找到所有为 1 的坐标

% ---------- 2. 把坐标存入 cell ----------
pairIdx = cell();                       % 初始化空 cell
for k = 1:length(ri)
    pairIdx{k} = {ri(k), ci(k)};        % 每对索引为 {行号, 列号}
end

% ---------- 3. （可选）若要同时捕获下三角（对称情况） ----------
% [L, ~] = tril(parallel_lines, -1);    % 下三角矩阵
% [rj, cj] = find(L == 1);
% for k = 1:length(rj)
%     pairIdx{end+1} = {rj(k), cj(k)}; % 再加入一次配对
% end

% -------------------------------------------------
% 现在 pairIdx 就是一个 cell 数组，里面存放了所有满足
% |C2(i)-C2(j)| < 0.5（即 parallel_lines(i,j)==1）的索引对
% -------------------------------------------------
disp(pairIdx);   % 查看结果
```

| 步骤 | 关键函数 | 作用 |
|------|----------|------|
| `triu(...,1)` | `triu` | 只保留上三角（不含对角线），避免同一对元素被重复计数 |
| `find(U==1)` | `find` | 取得所有值为 1 的坐标 `(ri,ci)` |
| `pairIdx{k} = {ri(k),ci(k)}` | 循环 | 把每对坐标存入 cell 数组 |
